report.intro-basic-desc: This inspection performs adaptation analysis for general open-source dependency libraries / self-developed source packages. The core basic information is shown in the table below. The dependency chain information includes the name, version and type of submodules, static libraries and dynamic libraries, fully covering the underlying dependency system of the inspected object.
report.intro-situation-desc: By means of a dedicated RISC-V AI cross-platform porting tool, this inspection performs a full scan of the inspected object and analyzes adaptability from two core dimensions: architecture-related files and architecture-related source code. It forms an overall conclusion on architecture-related code and provides targeted RISC-V replacement / adaptation suggestions.
report.intro-arch-file-desc: The architecture-related files identified by this inspection fall into four categories: source files, assembly source files, build system configuration files, and other files. The count, path, core function and adaptation level of each category are determined as follows:
report.intro-desc-1: This inspection is intended to resolve the compatibility issues of porting software / dependency libraries across architectures to RISC-V. Relying on the intelligent source-code analysis and precise architecture-related code recognition of the dedicated RISC-V AI cross-platform porting tool, it carries out full-dimensional porting adaptation inspection on the target source package / dependency library, and forms professional inspection results by locating architecture-related code and analyzing the code adaptation status.
report.intro-desc-2: This inspection covers the parseable source files of the target source package / dependency library and the complete dependency chain information (submodules / static libraries / dynamic libraries), excluding encapsulated-unparseable or encrypted code. The inspection results can serve as an intuitive reference for enterprises to estimate the workload and budget of RISC-V porting work, and also provide development teams with the technical direction and core basis for code modification in RISC-V porting adaptation.
report.declaration-1: 1. The validity of this report is based on the authenticity of the evidence provided by the inspected unit;
report.declaration-2: 2. Under no circumstances may the test results or conclusions referenced from this report be taken out of their original meaning, or be added to, modified, deleted, falsified or concealed in any way;
report.declaration-3: 3. If the application code exceeds the regular inspection standard in complexity due to multiple development languages, the organization will carry out the inspection according to the framework of the primary development language. The inspection scope is limited to the content explicitly described in this report and does not include unparsable encapsulated content or other unknown or undefined technical links.
